stem: Carrow Metals wants to know exactly where the record of their already-built infrastructure lives, before they have configured any remote backend. Where is it?

choices.text: Inside the `.tf` configuration files themselves, appended automatically at the end of every successful apply run.
In a local file named `terraform.tfstate` in the working directory, separate from the `.tf` configuration files.
In the dependency lock file, alongside the provider checksums.
Nowhere on disk; Terraform re-discovers all existing resources by querying every provider's API on each run.

rationale: Without a configured remote backend, state defaults to a local file named `terraform.tfstate`, kept separate from the `.tf` configuration files. Configuration files describe the desired end state and are not rewritten with built-infrastructure records after an apply. The dependency lock file only records provider versions and checksums, not resource state. Querying every provider's API on every run is exactly the performance problem a stored state file avoids.
